cls: Anti-IL-5 monoclonal antibody (interleukin-5 antagonist; humanized IgG1 kappa) - biologic
pharm: A humanized monoclonal antibody that binds and neutralizes interleukin-5 (IL-5), the key cytokine for eosinophil growth, activation, and survival, thereby reducing blood and tissue eosinophils as add-on maintenance therapy for eosinophilic diseases.
quick: Asthma/CRSwNP/COPD 100 mg SC q4w; EGPA/HES 300 mg SC q4w
Limited human data; IgG crosses placenta (more in 3rd trimester)
No data; maternal IgG present in milk; weigh benefit vs need
summary: Mepolizumab (Nucala) is a humanized IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody targeting interleukin-5 (IL-5), the principal cytokine for eosinophil differentiation, recruitment, activation, and survival. By binding circulating IL-5, it blocks IL-5 from attaching to the alpha chain of the IL-5 receptor on eosinophils, lowering eosinophil counts. It is given subcutaneously every 4 weeks as add-on maintenance therapy - not as a rescue or acute treatment. FDA indications are severe eosinophilic-phenotype asthma (age 6 and older), chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (adults), eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (adults), hypereosinophilic syndrome (age 12 and older, present 6 months or more without an identifiable non-hematologic secondary cause), and inadequately controlled eosinophilic-phenotype COPD (adults). It is supplied as a lyophilized powder for clinician administration, a prefilled syringe, and a prefilled autoinjector. Key safety considerations are hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis, herpes zoster (consider vaccination), and the need to treat pre-existing helminth infection before starting; corticosteroids should not be stopped abruptly.
indications: Add-on maintenance treatment of severe asthma with an eosinophilic phenotype in patients 6 years and older
Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps in adults
Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) in adults
Hypereosinophilic syndrome (HES) in patients 12 years and older for 6 months or more without an identifiable non-hematologic secondary cause
Inadequately controlled COPD with an eosinophilic phenotype in adults

dosage.n: Given as three separate 100 mg injections at least 5 cm apart
Given as three separate 100 mg injections

admin: Administer subcutaneously into the upper arm, thigh, or abdomen
Available as a 100 mg lyophilized powder vial (reconstituted and given by a healthcare provider), a prefilled autoinjector, and a prefilled syringe
For the 300 mg dose, give three separate 100 mg injections at least 5 cm (about 2 inches) apart
Reconstitute the lyophilized powder with 1.2 mL of Sterile Water for Injection to give 100 mg/mL; store the reconstituted solution below 30 C and discard if not used within 8 hours
Allow refrigerated prefilled devices to reach room temperature (about 30 minutes) before injecting; do not freeze
moa: Mepolizumab is an interleukin-5 (IL-5) antagonist monoclonal antibody (IgG1 kappa). IL-5 is the major cytokine driving eosinophil growth, differentiation, recruitment, activation, and survival. Mepolizumab binds soluble human IL-5 with high affinity and specificity, inhibiting its bioactivity by blocking IL-5 from binding to the alpha chain of the IL-5 receptor complex on the eosinophil surface. This reduces eosinophil production and survival, producing a marked dose-dependent reduction in blood and tissue eosinophil counts. The precise mechanism of its therapeutic effect in eosinophilic disease has not been definitively established.

absolute: History of hypersensitivity to mepolizumab or any excipient
relative: Acute bronchospasm or status asthmaticus (not for acute use)
Patients on systemic or inhaled corticosteroids that require gradual tapering
monitor: Hypersensitivity / anaphylaxis during and after injection
Disease control and avoidance of abrupt corticosteroid withdrawal

preg: Human data are insufficient; animal (cynomolgus monkey) studies showed no fetal harm up to about 9 times the maximum recommended human dose. As a monoclonal IgG antibody, mepolizumab crosses the placenta in increasing amounts as pregnancy progresses, particularly in the third trimester. A pregnancy exposure registry monitors outcomes.
lact: There are no data on the presence of mepolizumab in human milk, its effects on the breastfed infant, or its effect on milk production; maternal IgG is present in human milk. Weigh the benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and any potential effect on the infant.
renal: No dose adjustment is required; mepolizumab is not renally eliminated.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required; mepolizumab is not hepatically metabolized and is not a CYP450 substrate.

moderate: No formal drug-interaction studies have been performed; as a monoclonal antibody, mepolizumab is not expected to have CYP450-mediated interactions
minor: General biologic caution - avoid live vaccines without specialist advice
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction stated in labeling.
interactions.diagnostics: Expect a decline in blood eosinophil counts on treatment.

rare: Angioedema, bronchospasm, hypotension, urticaria associated with hypersensitivity
emergency: Anaphylaxis or severe allergic reaction (facial/mouth/tongue swelling, trouble breathing, hives, dizziness or fainting)

monitoring: Hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis during and after injection (especially early doses)
Signs of herpes zoster and eligibility for zoster vaccination before starting
Screen and treat helminth infection before initiation
Disease control and gradual corticosteroid taper
counsel: This is a maintenance medicine - it is NOT a rescue inhaler and must not be used for sudden breathing problems, acute attacks, or status asthmaticus
Do not stop your steroid medicines suddenly
Seek immediate care for signs of an allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, mouth, or tongue, trouble breathing, hives, or dizziness and fainting
Report symptoms of shingles, and ask your provider about vaccination
If self-injecting, follow the Instructions for Use, rotate sites (arm, thigh, abdomen), and for the 300 mg dose give three separate injections at least 2 inches apart
Take the device out of the fridge about 30 minutes before injecting to reach room temperature, and do not freeze it
pk: Eosinophil reduction begins within weeks; maintenance benefit over time
Tmax about 4-8 days after subcutaneous dosing; bioavailability ~80%
Dosed every 4 weeks; about 2-fold accumulation at steady state
Refrigerate 2-8 C, do not freeze, protect from light; unopened carton may be kept up to 30 C for up to 7 days
pearls: Anti-IL-5 antibody (binds the cytokine), in contrast to benralizumab (anti-IL-5 receptor alpha) and reslizumab (IV anti-IL-5)
Two dose levels: 100 mg for asthma, CRSwNP, and COPD; 300 mg (as three 100 mg injections) for EGPA and HES
Pediatric asthma (ages 6-11) uses a 40 mg dose
Reliable corticosteroid-sparing effect in EGPA and oral-corticosteroid-dependent eosinophilic asthma
Add-on maintenance only - not for acute attacks; treat any helminth infection before starting and consider zoster vaccination
missed: The label gives no specific algorithm. General practice is to give the missed dose as soon as possible and then resume the every-4-week schedule; do not double the dose, and confirm timing with the prescriber.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Single subcutaneous doses up to 1,500 mg in trials showed no dose-related toxicity. Manage supportively with appropriate monitoring.
